facts.fact: The Daily Nation reports the Court of Appeal struck down sections 22 and 23 of the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, 2018, but upheld sections 16, 17, 27, 28, 37 and investigative powers under sections 48 to 53, so the Act stands.

The Daily Nation says dozens of young social media users have faced arrests and prosecutions under the Act, increasing after the June 2024 protests, including teacher Albert Ojwang, arrested over a social media post and who died in custody in June 2025.
